episode_title: How an AI Army Replaced His Ad Agency (Up to $150K/Month in Spend)

real_qa.q: How does Airlock use GrokBot to automate ad creative production at scale?
real_qa.r: Airlock uses GrokBot with dedicated agents for specific areas, where each agent has its own dedicated computer and knows only its specific function. The platform integrates with Stefan Brain for direct response copywriting, Kling and Higgs Field for video generation, and AdNova for asset management. Once assets are uploaded to Slack, an Ad Launcher bot pulls them, identifies issues, hands off to a bot for headlines and descriptions, then a quality control bot trained on customer feedback reviews everything before the media buyer bot deploys campaigns to Meta and Google.

real_qa.q: What is Stefan Brain and how does it improve AI-generated ad copy compared to ChatGPT or Claude?
real_qa.r: Stefan Brain is a custom LLM platform trained by direct response copywriter and marketer Stefan Georgi. Plain Claude and plain OpenAI don't write good copy because the AI tries to close the loop and be smart, but Stefan Brain succeeds in generating copy that is at a decent good level and much better than plain Claude or OpenAI. Airlock connects their GrokBot to Stefan Brain via MCP to generate ad briefs based on angles and formats.
real_qa.requete: Stefan Brain direct response copywriting AI

real_qa.q: How does Airlock generate video B-roll using AI models like Kling instead of filming real boats and RVs?
real_qa.r: Airlock uses Kling and Higgs Field to generate video B-roll from reference images. They grab images from sources like CarMax for specific products and feed them to the model. Three to four years ago, they would need to find a boat in Fort Lauderdale, get permission, and record with their products on it, but now Kling can generate beautiful video of their products inside a boat or RV in exact conditions they specify. Kling is cheaper than Sora, which is why they use it more.
real_qa.requete: Kling AI video generation B-roll products

real_qa.q: What does Airlock's boomer bot quality control process do before launching ads to Meta?
real_qa.r: The boomer bot is trained on Airlock's customer feedback and how RV and boat owners speak. It reads all headlines, descriptions, and creative content to check if anything would trigger skepticism in their audience. For example, when they extended their guarantee from 90 days to 180 days for Black Friday, the boomer bot stopped an ad that still said 90 days and provided recommendations to the graphic designer for editing before launch.
real_qa.requete: quality control AI bots advertising Meta

real_qa.q: How many ad variations can Airlock now produce per week compared to before using AI agents?
real_qa.r: Before using AI, a video editor could make five video batches per week. Now they can make endless batches because the limitation is no longer production capacity but strategic decisions about whether they should do it, whether they have budget to test, and whether campaigns are set up correctly. The question shifted from 'can it be done' to 'should we do it' and Airlock can now press a button and have a hundred videos by tomorrow, though they may be 80% there rather than perfectly edited.
real_qa.requete: AI automation ad creative production speed

guest.bio_context: Mariano worked as a Software Engineer at Shopify on the point of sale mobile app using React Native while completing a Computer Science degree at the University of Florida. He was laid off during Shopify's 20-30% workforce reduction and transitioned full-time to Airlock, which he co-founded with a business partner who identified the need for air purification systems in the marine and RV markets. He studied for a Master's degree in Computer Science while testing Airlock full-time, then dropped the program after one year to focus entirely on the business.
